investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, so the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that expose the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, indicating the peer-pod VM quota on those nodes was fully consumed at scheduling time. The other 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector constraints. Preemption was also unavailable on both node groups. Because the pod remained unscheduled for 122 s (remote-agent-create), 142 s (remote-agent-state), and 146 s (remote-agent-runtime), the eval runner timed out before any VM was assigned, leaving all required evidence fields empty and causing all three checks to fail. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity constraint localized to the remote-agent Kubernetes node pool; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource quota exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: all available peer-pod VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime).

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only the 2 kata-capable nodes satisfy, so the effective scheduling pool is limited to those 2 nodes, amplifying the impact of any capacity shortfall.

Tertiary — peer-pod VM slots not released from a prior eval run or leaked agent: if a previous remote-agent probe did not clean up its VM allocation, the slots may remain consumed. The withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1883) is intended to handle this, but a prior crash or timeout could have bypassed cleanup.

Lower confidence — node pool under-provisioned for concurrent eval load: if multiple eval runs or production workloads compete for the same 2 kata-capable nodes simultaneously, transient exhaustion could occur without a persistent leak.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api between 14:44 and 14:49 UTC on 2026-07-06 with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule new kata peer-pod VMs because 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the eval runner calls createAgent with type "remote" as its first step (run-status-probes.mjs line 1905), the pod never became schedulable, the agent was never created, and no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written, causing a complete contract gap against the expected-output contract defined at check-expectations.json line 264.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the kata peer-pod VM required to back a remote agent. Of the 6 available nodes, 2 reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm (the resource quota or node-level VM slot pool is exhausted) and 4 did not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity constraint, not an application code defect. Because agent creation is a prerequisite for all three remote-agents checks, the capacity exhaustion caused a cascading failure across the entire remote-agents feature: remote-agent-create failed first (endedAt 14:44:08), remote-agent-state failed next (endedAt 14:46:34), and remote-agent-runtime failed last (endedAt 14:49:05). This is an eval-observed infrastructure failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary (high confidence): kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota or node-level VM slot pool is exhausted on the 2 nodes that support peer-pod scheduling, preventing any new remote agent pod from being placed. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message).

Secondary (high confidence): The remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector rules, meaning they are structurally ineligible for peer-pod workloads regardless of capacity, further reducing the schedulable node pool to zero.

Tertiary (medium confidence): A prior eval run or a concurrent workload may have consumed all available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots without releasing them, leaving no headroom for the probe's agent pod. The eval runner uses withCleanup (run-status-probes.mjs line 1903), but if a previous run leaked a VM slot, capacity would not have been restored.

Lower confidence: A node affinity/selector misconfiguration or a recent change to node labels could have reduced the set of eligible nodes from more than 2 to exactly 2, making the cluster more sensitive to VM slot exhaustion. No suspect changes in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges support this hypothesis at this time.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, so the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that expose the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, indicating the peer-pod VM quota on those nodes was fully consumed at scheduling time. The other 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector constraints. Preemption was also unavailable on both node groups. Because the pod remained unscheduled for 122 s (remote-agent-create), 142 s (remote-agent-state), and 146 s (remote-agent-runtime), the eval runner timed out before any VM was assigned, leaving all required evidence fields empty and causing all three checks to fail. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity constraint localized to the remote-agent Kubernetes node pool; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: 'pod stuck unscheduled for 122s (Unschedulable): 0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'

sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical Unschedulable reason, pod stuck for 146 s, zero evidence collected.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}) — no orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState was written, consistent with the pod never reaching a running state.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all 4 required evidence keys (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent, confirming the probe never progressed past pod scheduling.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885; a scheduling failure before VM assignment would prevent any evidence from being written.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent === true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready']; neither assertion could be evaluated because the pod was never scheduled.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=129570 — the probe ran for ~129 s before failing, consistent with the scheduler's 122 s unschedulable window reported in the message.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource quota exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: all available peer-pod VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime).

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only the 2 kata-capable nodes satisfy, so the effective scheduling pool is limited to those 2 nodes, amplifying the impact of any capacity shortfall.

Tertiary — peer-pod VM slots not released from a prior eval run or leaked agent: if a previous remote-agent probe did not clean up its VM allocation, the slots may remain consumed. The withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1883) is intended to handle this, but a prior crash or timeout could have bypassed cleanup.

Lower confidence — node pool under-provisioned for concurrent eval load: if multiple eval runs or production workloads compete for the same 2 kata-capable nodes simultaneously, transient exhaustion could occur without a persistent leak.

investigations.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api between 14:44 and 14:49 UTC on 2026-07-06 with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule new kata peer-pod VMs because 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the eval runner calls createAgent with type "remote" as its first step (run-status-probes.mjs line 1905), the pod never became schedulable, the agent was never created, and no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written, causing a complete contract gap against the expected-output contract defined at check-expectations.json line 264.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the kata peer-pod VM required to back a remote agent. Of the 6 available nodes, 2 reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm (the resource quota or node-level VM slot pool is exhausted) and 4 did not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity constraint, not an application code defect. Because agent creation is a prerequisite for all three remote-agents checks, the capacity exhaustion caused a cascading failure across the entire remote-agents feature: remote-agent-create failed first (endedAt 14:44:08), remote-agent-state failed next (endedAt 14:46:34), and remote-agent-runtime failed last (endedAt 14:49:05). This is an eval-observed infrastructure failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Remote-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in sequence between 14:44 and 14:49 UTC on 2026-07-06 with identical Kubernetes scheduling errors: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval's remote-agent pod because 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the agent was never created, and the eval runner never received any response evidence, causing a total contract gap (all 5 required fields — orgId, agentId, model, provider, message — are missing).
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster serving the production-api remote-agent workload has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that match the pod's affinity/selector. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state) confirms that no schedulable node exists for the remote-agent pod type. This is a Kubernetes infrastructure-layer failure localized to the kata peer-pods VM resource pool, not an application code defect. No evidence of a user-facing incident or real-traffic impact is present in the packet; this is an eval-detected infrastructure failure.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1910-1918: the runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1918; if the pod cannot be scheduled, createAgent never returns a usable agent and no evidence can be collected.

source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:181-189: remote-agent-runtime is registered as required=false with outageLatencyMs=420000; the observed latency of 151076ms is well under the outage threshold, confirming the failure is a hard scheduling block rather than a latency breach.
possibleCauses: Most likely — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool exhausted on the 2 affinity-matching nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing pods and no preemption victims were found, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods. Supported directly by all three check messages.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not match the pod's affinity/selector, meaning only 2 nodes are even eligible, amplifying the impact of any capacity shortfall. If the affinity rules were recently tightened or node labels changed, the effective schedulable pool shrank.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning for the remote-agent workload: the cluster has only 6 nodes total, with only 2 carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource, providing no redundancy when those 2 nodes are saturated.

Lower confidence — a transient spike in concurrent remote-agent pod creation (e.g., from other eval runs or user traffic) consumed all kata.peerpods.io/vm slots just before this eval window, causing temporary exhaustion rather than a permanent capacity deficit.

whatWouldDisproveThis: A re-run of the eval that succeeds (pod schedules, agent is created, all 5 evidence fields are present) would disprove that the capacity issue is persistent and suggest a transient spike.

kubectl describe node output showing kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity is not exhausted on the 2 affinity-matching nodes would disprove the resource exhaustion hypothesis and point to a different scheduling constraint.
Evidence that the pod affinity/selector rules changed and now match zero nodes (rather than 2) would shift the primary cause from resource exhaustion to affinity misconfiguration.

A passing run of remote-agent-create or remote-agent-state at the same time as the runtime failure would disprove the shared-infrastructure hypothesis and suggest the runtime check has an isolated issue.

User-traffic or incident signals showing remote agent provisioning succeeding for real users during this window would indicate the failure is isolated to the eval probe's service account, namespace, or resource quota rather than the shared kata VM pool.

Add a post-run cleanup verification eval that confirms no remote-agent pods from prior eval runs remain in a Running or Pending state after the withCleanup window, detecting slot leakage.

Consider a canary eval that attempts to schedule a minimal remote-agent pod on a short timeout (e.g., 30s) as a lightweight pre-check before the full remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime evals run, enabling faster failure detection with less resource consumption.
